listing.name: Star Wars: Rogue Squadron 64 Recompiled
listing.summary: Native Rogue Squadron 64 source build for your own USA v1.0 original. Complete upstream RT64/toolchain preparation and keep the original in the launch working folder. The documented Windows game output is RogueSquadron64Recomp.exe; optional Steam relay has separate SDK/runtime prerequisites.

steps.title: Prepare upstream or keep an existing game build
steps.instruction: Use a privately built player from the pinned upstream instructions with your own Star Wars: Rogue Squadron USA v1.0 original. Supply rogue_squadron.z64, rogue_squadron.v64 or rogue_squadron.n64 for the upstream import. Keep the build tools and optional Steam relay separate from the game program.

steps.title: Keep your files and update through upstream
steps.instruction: Keep the game in a separate folder you control, and retain a working copy. Review its executable in Portcove, then add it without changing its files. Choose Play separately when you are ready. You manage updates, original files, generated data, saves and settings. Portcove does not replace, back up or roll back this external copy. Follow the project’s instructions for the version you use when changing it.

references.title: Build the desktop player for your system
references.instruction: Follow the pinned upstream build instructions for Windows or Linux. Use your own USA v1.0 ROM with normalized xxHash3 0x6B66A44153594DEA. For a direct build, select the completed RogueSquadron64Recomp player and use the prepared working folder. The game imports the ROM and keeps its profile in that folder.

references.title: Find the profile for a Linux package you built
references.instruction: The upstream AppImage uses ~/.local/share/RogueSquadron64Recomp by default, with RS64_DATA_DIR as an override. The Flatpak uses ~/.var/app/io.github.MikeSemicolonD.RogueSquadron64Recomp/data. Keep the effective folder and launch the complete package using its own setup instructions.

references.title: Keep desktop and Mac profiles separate
references.instruction: Preserve saves/rs64.n64.us.1.0.bin, the imported ROM, settings, mods and logs. The upstream Mac cross-build targets Intel and Apple silicon with Metal. An app bundle uses the SDL RogueSquadron64Recomp folder under Application Support when available and copies bundled mods there. Use the effective folder and preserve custom mods before changing builds. Native Mac startup remains unverified.

references.title: Build and import on Android
references.instruction: Run the upstream Windows Debug build first to generate the Android build inputs, then use the Gradle instructions with NDK 29.0.14206865. The ARM64 app requires Android 9 or later with Vulkan 1.1. Select your own ROM with the app’s file picker. The app validates and imports it. Preserve the effective com.rs64recomp.app files folder and its saves, mods and roguesq_touch.json. The app can fall back to internal storage.
